parsed.why: State-directed targeting: police register of LGBTIQ people, lured-meeting entrapment, extortion and raids, with police inaction on forced marriages. No anti-discrimination protection and no working advocacy access. Severe tier-2 exposure.

Thin data. Decriminalised by court in 2022 with no post-repeal protections. Official 2005 port exclusion and 'no mandate' stance are dated. Police avoided as a reporting route. No documented trans-specific targeting, so the score sits in the middle.

Gender identity protected since 2013 with a 2024 damages ruling and a 2025 hate-crime law. Same-sex marriage and recognition in place. Main exposures are prison admission by gender identity with surgery exclusion, youth-care restrictions and contested facilities rules. Strong rule of law.

Custody placed by birth or legal sex, with trans women in male pavilions and documented harms and deaths. Violence rising amid armed conflict, with 27 LGBTQ murders in 2023 but no denominator. Offsets are self-determined legal recognition and authorised pride marches. Adoption ban is resident-facing.

Hate-crime and labour protections on gender identity, plus police training and guidelines addressing trans detainees by identified gender. Dated attacks (2001–2014) and dated survey data. Police still disregard complaints, and society is strongly heteronormative. Protections are fragmented.
